title: Redwood structured output + function/tool calling demo - Novus Retail
summary: AE+SE demo of Redwood structured output (JSON mode), function/tool calling, and guardrails. Covered API example, Console UI for schema enforcement, Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, security questions (SOC 2, KMS, VPC). Agreed next steps: send security pack, price estimate for Dedicated + POC, schedule POC kickoff.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Nguyen (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Novus - Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Novus - Platform), Priya Menon (Novus - CTO)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, Samir from Redwood, thanks for making time. Quick check — audio ok for folks?
[00:07] Maya: Yep good here, thanks.
[00:10] Jules: Hi all, Jules on the SE side, I'll run the technical demo and answer infra questions.
[00:18] Samir: Awesome. High level — 30-ish minute walkthrough of structured output and function/tool calling, then Q&A and POC scoping. Does that work?
[00:26] Priya: Sounds good. We're particularly interested in enforcing JSON schemas and safe tool invocation patterns.
[00:33] Samir: Great, we'll show JSON mode and the Console guardrails, plus an API example you can replicate.

Auto-summary (may be imperfect):
- Demo showed JSON mode with explicit schema enforcement and fallback behavior.
- Function calling for internal tools (inventory lookup, pricing calc) demoed; discussed safety/authorization.
- Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted for latency/cost and VPC options.

[02:00] Jules: Ok jumping into the Console. First slide — here's the structured output mode, you can attach a JSON schema that the model must follow. Internally Redwood validates token stream against schema and will emit an error or fallback if the model drifts.
[02:22] Carlos: When you say "validate token stream" — is that post-hoc or streaming-valid? We need streaming detection to stop downstream parsers.
[02:33] Jules: Good Q. We do a hybrid: schema checks on the streamed output and we can attach an automatic repair policy — e.g., attempt n retries or call a sanitizer function. There's also a strict mode which will return a non-200 and an error payload if the schema is violated.
[02:52] Maya: Any examples?
[02:55] Jules: Yep, here's a quick API snippet in the Console: request body includes "response_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{...}} and "mode":"json". I'll paste the snippet in chat after the meeting, but here's the mental model — output must match shape, types, field enums, etc.

[05:10] Samir: Also want to note guardrails — you can define field-level validators, max tokens per field, and required fields. For tool-calling we surface the function spec.
[05:23] Priya: How deterministic is it? If a model returns a slight variant like single quotes or extra commas, what's the behavior?
[05:35] Jules: So transcription note — we sometimes call this "json-mode with lenient parsing". By default we do strict JSON parse, but Console offers a tolerant parser that attempts to correct for common model errors (extra commas, single quotes) before failing. You can tune that.

[07:40] Maya: Let's talk about function calling. We want the LLM to call our internal inventory API only for authorized SKUs and never return raw PII.
[07:52] Jules: Right — function calling workflow: you register function definitions (name, input schema, output schema), Redwood will surface them to the model as callable endpoints. You can attach RBAC and a gateway to control which functions a model can call and under what client context. We demo an inventory_lookup function.
[08:18] Carlos: Do you do authentication headers injection or do we need a sidecar?
[08:24] Jules: We support injecting short-lived service tokens generated by your KMS/HSM or our token broker depending on deployment. In Private deployments you can keep tokens on-prem. We log function invocations in audit logs for traceability.

[10:00] Samir: Quick live demo — I'll call the hosted API in JSON mode to produce an order summary and then trigger a price_calculator function. Jules, can you share your screen for the Console flow?
[10:12] Jules: Sharing.
[10:20] [10:20] Jules: Here's the Console schema panel. I'm pasting a schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}}}} — bear with my chatty demo fingers, sometimes the Console preview lags.
[10:48] Maya: I'm seeing the preview — interesting, do you have built-in examples for nested arrays?
[10:53] Jules: Yes, you can supply examples that the runtime uses as few-shot context or for a sanity-check.

[12:10] [12:10] Jules: Now function calling. I'm sending the same prompt but with a function spec for price_calculator. The model will output a call payload rather than final text. Here's the function signature in the Console: name, parameters schema, and execution endpoint.
[12:38] Carlos: If the model suggests calling an unauthorized function, how do you prevent it?
[12:45] Jules: At routing time we filter available function specs based on request policy — e.g., customer tier, route config, or ephemeral POC tokens. So the model only sees allowed function meta.

[15:00] Priya: Security questions — SOC 2 status, KMS integration, VPC peering, audit log retention?
[15:08] Samir: We're SOC 2 Type II. For KMS we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for Private. VPC peering + private endpoints supported on Dedicated and Private. Audit logs are available in Console and can be forwarded to your SIEM. I'll send the security pack — includes SOC 2 report, pen test summary, and diagram of key flows.

[17:30] Maya: On fidelity — how do you measure hallucination risk when using structured output? If the model invents SKUs, how's that caught?
[17:42] Jules: Two things: schema enforcement prevents wrong types/fields, but not necessarily invented values. So we recommend function-calling to do authoritative lookups for canonical SKU data. Redwood Optimize can also run evals on your prompt set and surface regression alerts — e.g., if SKU mismatch rate increases.

[20:00] Samir: Pricing tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated vs private. Hosted is quickest and cheaper for adhoc, but Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token costs at scale and Private gives you full network control. For a transactional retail workload where latency matters, Dedicated in a nearby region is often chosen.
[20:32] Priya: Any latency SLOs you achieve? We're aiming sub-200ms for simple lookups.
[20:39] Jules: On typical small model variants and optimized runtime, many customers see 50-150ms p50 for short sequences; large seq heatmaps increase. We can run a benchmark with your request profile as part of the POC.

[23:10] Carlos: About logs — can we redact PII automatically prior to storing?
[23:18] Samir: Yes, you can configure redact policies in the Console pipeline; Redwood also supports client-side tokenization and selective logging for Private. We provide hooks to scrub fields before persistence.

[25:00] Maya: Ok can we talk POC? Our success criteria: 1) integrated JSON output matching our order schema 95% of the time across 5k test prompts, 2) function calling reliably invokes inventory without leaks, 3) latency under 250ms p95 for 100rps. Timeline: want a 4-week POC starting mid-May if feasible.
[25:28] Samir: That sounds reasonable. Typical POC: 2-week integration + 2-week load/quality testing. We can provide a Dedicated trial pool for the POC. I'll follow up with a scope doc and quote.

[28:00] Jules: Demo note — here's an example function call payload the model emits: {name: "price_calculator", args: {items: [...]}}. Our executor calls your endpoint with the validated args. If the function returns an error, we surface that in the model context and can trigger a fallback model or sanitized message.
[28:35] Maya: Does Redwood store the function outputs? We need to keep some responses ephemeral.
[28:42] Jules: You can configure persistence per-route: ephemeral-only, or stored with encryption. Audit logs still capture invocation metadata unless you disable them for the route.

[31:00] Carlos: Competitors question — we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI; curious where Redwood is stronger.
[31:08] Samir: Great question. Redwood focuses on inference serving and operational tooling — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, built-in batching/caching (KV cache optimization), and native schema+function tooling. Some vendors are strong on models but less opinionated on production rollouts and cost controls.
[31:32] Maya: Are there any partner-managed deployments — like managed Dedicated in our cloud?
[31:38] Samir: Yes we have partner options and marketplace listings. For regulated workloads we recommend Private with your VPC.

[34:00] Priya: A couple of nitty bits — how do you handle model upgrades and rollbacks during POC?
[34:10] Jules: The Console supports pinned model versions per-route, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to a previous model or smaller variant if latency or error rates spike. We'll keep audit trail of rollouts.

[36:50] Samir: I'm going to summarize next steps now and capture action items.
[36:57] Maya: Perfect.

[37:05] Samir: Next steps: 1) We send security pack + SOC2 + KMS diagrams, 2) Samir to share POC scope and pricing for Dedicated trial, 3) Jules to share API snippets and Console export of schema examples, 4) schedule POC kickoff for week of May 11. Any objections?
[37:28] Priya: No objections, that's aligned.

[38:10] Maya: Action item — we'll provide a sample of 5k test prompts and our order schema by Apr 24.
[38:18] Carlos: I'll coordinate infra for endpoint access and will need the token lifecycle details.

[40:00] Jules: I'll put the function spec examples and the tolerant parser knobs into the repo link in chat. Note: sometimes keys in examples get mangled in the transcript — I'll double-check the exported snippet.

[42:30] Samir: One more note on cost optimization: Redwood Optimize recommendations will suggest batching sizes and quantization profiles based on your seq length distribution; we can include that in the POC report.

[44:00] Priya: Any privacy/legal asks for the early POC?
[44:06] Samir: We'll sign an MSA addendum and an NDA if needed, but for smaller POCs we often run under a trial agreement and share limited data. Legal can coordinate after we send the SOW.

[46:30] Maya: Quick question — does structured output support enums and conditional fields? e.g., if payment_method=="gift_card" then gift_card_code required.
[46:42] Jules: Yes, you can express those via JSON Schema conditional keywords or use pre-exec validators that assert business logic. We also do runtime checks and can return structured error info.

[49:00] Samir: Ok final recap — we'll send: security pack, POC scope & pricing, API/Console snippets, and propose May 11 kickoff. Customer to send sample prompts and schema by Apr 24.
[49:18] Priya: Thanks, that works.
[51:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, appreciate the demo. We'll review and get back.
[51:40] Samir: Thanks all, talk soon.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present (function names sometimes hyphenated, product names may appear as "Red wood"). References to artifacts: security pack link (sent in follow-up), demo deck (link), console snippets (exported).
